text: These Regulations may be cited as the Network and Information Systems Regulations 2018 and come into force on 10th May 2018.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In these Regulations— “cloud computing service” means a digital service that enables access to a scalable and elastic pool of shareable computing resources; “the Commission” means the Commission of the European Union; “Cooperation Group” means the group established under Article 11(1); “CSIRTs network” means the network established under Article 12(1); “digital service” means a service within the meaning of point (b) of Article 1(1) of Directive 2015/1535 which is of any the following kinds—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: online marketplace;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: online search engine;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: cloud computing service; “digital service provider” means any person who provides a digital service; “Directive 2013/11” means Directive 2013/11/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council on alternative dispute resolution for consumer disputes(a), and amending Regulation (EC) No 2006/2004 and Directive 2009/22/EC, as amended from time to time; “Directive 2015/1535” means Directive (EU) 2015/1535 of the European Parliament and of the Council laying down a procedure for the provision of information in the field of technical regulations and of rules on Information Society services(b), as amended from time to time; “Directive 2016/1148” means Directive (EU) 2016/1148 of the European Parliament and of the Council concerning measures for a high common level of security of network and information systems across the Union(c), as amended from time to time; “Drinking Water Quality Regulator for Scotland” means the person appointed by the Scottish Ministers under section 7(1) of the Water Industry (Scotland) Act 2002(d); “essential service” means a service which is essential for the maintenance of critical societal or economic activities; “GCHQ” means the Government Communications Headquarters within the meaning of section 3 of the Intelligence Services Act 1994(e); “incident” means any event having an actual adverse effect on the security of network and information systems; “network and information system” (“NIS”) means—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: an electronic communications network within the meaning of section 32(1) of the Communications Act 2003(f);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: any device or group of interconnected or related devices, one or more of which, pursuant to a program, perform automatic processing of digital data; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: digital data stored, processed, retrieved or transmitted by elements covered under paragraph (a) or (b) for the purposes of their operation, use, protection and maintenance; “online marketplace” means a digital service that allows consumers and/or traders as respectively defined in point (a) and in point (b) of Article 4(1) of Directive 2013/11 to conclude online sales or service contracts with traders either on the online marketplace’s website or on a trader’s website that uses computing services provided by the online marketplace; “online search engine” means a digital service that allows users to perform searches of, in principle, all websites or websites in a particular language on the basis of a query on any subject in the form of a keyword, phrase or other input, and returns links in which information related to the requested content can be found; “operator of an essential service” (“OES”) means a person who is deemed to be designated as an operator of an essential service under regulation 8(1) or is designated as an operator of an essential service under regulation 8(3); “relevant law-enforcement authority” has the meaning given in section 63A(1A) of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984(a); and “risk” means any reasonably identifiable circumstance or event having a potential adverse effect on the security of network and information systems.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In these Regulations a reference to—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: an Article, Annex, paragraph of an Article or Annex is a reference to the Article, Annex of paragraph as numbered in Directive 2016/1148;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: a numbered regulation, paragraph or Schedule is a reference to the regulation, paragraph or Schedule as numbered in these Regulations;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “the relevant authorities in a Member State” is a reference to the designated single point of contact (“SPOC”), computer security incident response team (“CSIRT”) and national competent authorities for that Member State;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the “designated competent authority for an operator of an essential service” is a reference to the competent authority that is designated under regulation 3(1) for the subsector in relation to which that operator provides an essential service;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: a “relevant digital service provider” (“RDSP”) is a reference to a person who provides a digital service in the United Kingdom and satisfies the following conditions—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the head office for that provider is in the United Kingdom or that provider has nominated a representative who is established in the United Kingdom;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the provider is not a micro or small enterprise as defined in Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC(b);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the “NIS enforcement authorities” is a reference to the competent authorities designated under regulation 3(1) and the Information Commissioner;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “security of network and information systems” means the ability of network and information systems to resist, at a given level of confidence, any action that compromises the availability, authenticity, integrity or confidentiality of stored or transmitted or processed data or the related services offered by, or accessible via, those network and information systems.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Expressions and words used in these Regulations which are also used in Directive 2016/1148 have the same meaning as in Directive 2016/1148.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Nothing in these Regulations prevents a person from taking an action (or not taking an action) which that person considers is necessary for the purposes of safeguarding the United Kingdom’s essential State functions, in particular—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: safeguarding national security, including protecting information the disclosure of which the person considers is contrary to the essential interests of the United Kingdom’s security; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: maintaining law and order, in particular, to allow for the investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences(c).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: These Regulations apply to—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the United Kingdom, including its internal waters;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the territorial sea adjacent to the United Kingdom;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the sea (including the seabed and subsoil) in any area designated under section 1(7) of the Continental Shelf Act 1964(a).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A Minister of the Crown must designate and publish a strategy to provide strategic objectives and priorities on the security of network and information systems in the United Kingdom (“the NIS national strategy”).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The strategic objectives and priorities set out in the NIS national strategy must be aimed at achieving and maintaining a high level of security of network and information systems in—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the sectors specified in column 1 of the table in Schedule 1 (“the relevant sectors”); and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: digital services.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The NIS national strategy may be published in such form and manner as the Minister considers appropriate.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The NIS national strategy may be reviewed by the Minister at any time and, if it is revised following such a review, the Minister must designate and publish a revised NIS national strategy as soon as reasonably practicable following that review.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The NIS national strategy must, in particular, address the following matters—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the regulatory measures and enforcement framework to secure the objectives and priorities of the strategy;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the roles and responsibilities of the key persons responsible for implementing the strategy;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the measures relating to preparedness, response and recovery, including cooperation between public and private sectors;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: education, awareness-raising and training programmes relating to the strategy;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: research and development plans relating to the strategy;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: a risk assessment plan identifying any risks; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: a list of the persons involved in the implementation of the strategy.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The Minister must communicate the NIS national strategy, including any revised NIS national strategy, to the Commission within three months after the date on which the strategy is designated under paragraph (1).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Before publishing the NIS national strategy or communicating it to the Commission, the Minister may redact any part of it which relates to national security.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In this regulation “a Minister of the Crown” has the same meaning as in section 8(1) of the Ministers of the Crown Act 1975(b).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The person specified in column 3 of the table in Schedule 1 is designated as the competent authority, for the territorial jurisdiction indicated in that column, and for the subsector specified in column 2 of that table (“the designated competent authorities”).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The Information Commissioner is designated as the competent authority for the United Kingdom for RDSPs.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In relation to the subsector for which it is designated under paragraph (1), the competent authority must—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: review the application of these Regulations;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: prepare and publish guidance;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: keep a list of all the operators of essential services who are designated, or deemed to be designated, under regulation 8, including an indication of the importance of each operator in relation to the subsector in relation to which it provides an essential service;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: keep a list of all the revocations made under regulation 9;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: send a copy of the lists mentioned in sub-paragraphs (c) and (d) to GCHQ, as the SPOC designated under regulation 4, to enable it to prepare the report mentioned in regulation 4(3);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: consult and co-operate with the Information Commissioner when addressing incidents that result in breaches of personal data; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in order to fulfil the requirements of these Regulations, consult and co-operate with—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: relevant law-enforcement authorities;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: competent authorities in other Member States;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: other competent authorities in the United Kingdom;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the SPOC that is designated under regulation 4; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the CSIRT that is designated under regulation 5.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In relation to digital services, the Information Commissioner must—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: review the application of these Regulations;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: prepare and publish guidance; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: consult and co-operate with the persons mentioned in paragraph (3)(g), in order to fulfil the requirements of these Regulations.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The guidance that is published by under paragraph (3)(b) or (4)(b) may be—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: published in such form and manner as the competent authority or Information Commissioner considers appropriate; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: reviewed at any time, and if it is revised following such a review, the competent authority or Information Commissioner must publish revised guidance as soon as reasonably practicable.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The competent authorities designated under paragraph (1) and the Information Commissioner must have regard to the national strategy that is published under regulation 2(1) when carrying out their duties under these Regulations.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: GCHQ is designated as the SPOC on the security of network and information systems for the United Kingdom.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The SPOC must—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: liaise with the relevant authorities in other Member States, the Cooperation Group and the CSIRTs network to ensure cross-border co-operation;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: consult and co-operate, as it considers appropriate, with relevant law-enforcement authorities; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: co-operate with the NIS enforcement authorities to enable the enforcement authorities to fulfil their obligations under these Regulations.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The SPOC must submit reports to—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the Cooperation Group based on the incident reports it received under regulation 11(9) and 12(15), including the number of notifications and the nature of notified incidents; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the Commission identifying the number of operators of essential services for each subsector listed in Schedule 2, indicating their importance in relation to that sector.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The first report mentioned in paragraph (3)(a) must be submitted on or before 9th August 2018 and subsequent reports must be submitted at annual intervals.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The first report mentioned in paragraph (3)(b) must be submitted on or before 9th November 2018 and subsequent reports must be submitted at biennial intervals.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: GCHQ is designated as the CSIRT for the United Kingdom in respect of the relevant sectors and digital services.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The CSIRT must—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: monitor incidents in the United Kingdom;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: provide early warning, alerts, announcements and dissemination of information to relevant stakeholders about risks and incidents;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: respond to any incident notified to it under regulation 11(5)(b) or regulation 12(8);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: provide dynamic risk and incident analysis and situational awareness;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: participate and co-operate in the CSIRTs network;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: establish relationships with the private sector to facilitate co-operation with that sector;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: promote the adoption and use of common or standardised practices for—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: incident and risk handling procedures, and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: incident, risk and information classification schemes; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: co-operate with NIS enforcement authorities to enable the enforcement authorities to fulfil their obligations under these Regulations.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The CSIRT may participate in international co-operation networks if the CSIRT considers it appropriate to do so.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The NIS enforcement authorities may share information with the CSIRT, the Commission and the relevant authorities in other Member States if that information sharing is—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: necessary for the requirements of these Regulations, and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: limited to information which is relevant and proportionate to the purpose of the information sharing.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: When sharing information with the Commission or the relevant authorities in other Member States under paragraph (1), the NIS enforcement authorities are not required to share—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: confidential information, or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: information which may prejudice the security or commercial interests of operators of essential services or digital service providers.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In order to facilitate the exercise of the Northern Ireland competent authority’s functions under these Regulations—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: a Northern Ireland Department may share information with the Northern Ireland competent authority; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the Northern Ireland competent authority may share information with a Northern Ireland Department.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In this regulation—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “the Northern Ireland competent authority” means the competent authority that is specified for Northern Ireland in column 3 of the table in Schedule 1 in relation to the subsectors specified in column 2 of that table; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “a Northern Ireland Department” means a department mentioned in Schedule 1 to the Departments Act (Northern Ireland) 2016(a).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: If a person provides an essential service of a kind referred to in paragraphs 1 to 9 of Schedule 2 and that service— that person is deemed to be designated as an OES for the subsector that is specified with respect to that essential service in that Schedule.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: relies on network and information systems; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: satisfies a threshold requirement described for that kind of essential service,
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A person who falls within paragraph (1) must notify the designated competent authority of that fact before the notification date.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Even if a person does not meet the threshold requirement mentioned in paragraph (1)(b), a competent authority may designate that person as an OES for the subsector in relation to which that competent authority is designated under regulation 3(1), if the following conditions are met—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: that person provides an essential service of a kind specified in paragraphs 1 to 9 of Schedule 2 for the subsector in relation to which the competent authority is designated under regulation 3(1);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the provision of that essential service by that person relies on network and information systems; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the competent authority concludes that an incident affecting the provision of that essential service by that person is likely to have significant disruptive effects on the provision of the essential service.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In order to arrive at the conclusion mentioned in paragraph (3)(c), the competent authority must have regard to the following factors—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the number of users relying on the service provided by the person;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the degree of dependency of the other relevant sectors on the service provided by that person;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the likely impact of incidents on the essential service provided by that person, in terms of its degree and duration, on economic and societal activities or public safety;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the market share of the essential service provided by that person;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the geographical area that may be affected if an incident impacts on the service provided by that person;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the importance of the provision of the service by that person for maintaining a sufficient level of that service, taking into account the availability of alternative means of essential service provision;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the likely consequences for national security if an incident impacts on the service provided by that person; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: any other factor the competent authority considers appropriate to have regard to, in order to arrive at a conclusion under this paragraph.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A competent authority must designate an OES under paragraph (3) by notice in writing served on the person who is to be designated and provide reasons for the designation in the notice.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Before a competent authority designates a person as an OES under paragraph (3), the authority may—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: request information from that person under regulation 15(4); and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: invite the person to submit any written representations about the proposed decision to designate it as an OES.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A competent authority must consult with the relevant authorities in another Member State before designating a person as an OES under paragraph (3) if that person already provides an essential service in that Member State.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A competent authority must maintain a list of all the persons who are deemed to be designated under paragraph (1) or designated under paragraph (3) for the subsectors in relation to which that competent authority is designated under regulation 3(1).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The competent authority must review the list mentioned in paragraph (8) at regular intervals and in accordance with paragraph (10).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The first review under paragraph (9) must take place before 9th May 2020, and subsequent reviews must take place, at least, biennially.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In this regulation the “notification” date means—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: 10th August 2018, in the case of a person who falls within paragraph (1) on the date these Regulations come into force; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in any other case, the date three months after the date on which the person falls within that paragraph.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Even if a person satisfies the threshold mentioned in regulation 8(1)(b), a relevant competent authority may revoke the deemed designation of that person, by notice, if the authority concludes that an incident affecting the provision of that essential service by that person is not likely to have significant disruptive effects on the provision of the essential service.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A competent authority may revoke a designation of a person under regulation 8(3), by notice, if the conditions mentioned in that regulation are no longer met by that person.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Before revoking a deemed designation of a person under regulation 8(1), or a designation of a person under regulation 8(3), the competent authority must—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: serve a notice in writing of proposed revocation on that person;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: provide reasons for the proposed decision;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: invite that person to submit any written representations about the proposed decision within such time period as may be specified by the competent authority; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: consider any representations submitted by the person under sub-paragraph (c) before a final decision is taken to revoke the designation.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In order to arrive at the conclusion mentioned in paragraph (1), the competent authority must have regard to the factors mentioned in regulation 8(4).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A competent authority may revoke a deemed designation under regulation 8(1), or a designation of a person under regulation 8(3), if the authority has received a request from another Member State to do so and the competent authority is in agreement that the designation of that person should be revoked.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: An OES must take appropriate and proportionate technical and organisational measures to manage risks posed to the security of the network and information systems on which their essential service relies.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: An OES must take appropriate and proportionate measures to prevent and minimise the impact of incidents affecting the security of the network and information systems used for the provision of an essential service, with a view to ensuring the continuity of those services.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The measures taken under paragraph (1) must, having regard to the state of the art, ensure a level of security of network and information systems appropriate to the risk posed.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Operators of essential services must have regard to any relevant guidance issued by the relevant competent authority when carrying out their duties imposed by paragraphs (1) and (2).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: An OES must notify the designated competent authority about any incident which has a significant impact on the continuity of the essential service which that OES provides (“a network and information systems (“NIS”) incident”).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In order to determine the significance of the impact of an incident an OES must have regard to the following factors—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the number of users affected by the disruption of the essential service;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the duration of the incident; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the geographical area affected by the incident.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The notification mentioned in paragraph (1) must—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: provide the following—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the operator’s name and the essential services it provides;

text: the time the NIS incident occurred;

text: information concerning any, or any likely, cross-border impact of the NIS incident; and

text: any other information that may be helpful to the competent authority; and

text: be provided to the competent authority—

text: without undue delay and in any event no later than 72 hours after the operator is aware that a NIS incident has occurred; and

text: in such form and manner as the competent authority determines.
