text: The information to be provided by an OES under paragraph (3)(a) is limited to information which may reasonably be expected to be within the knowledge of that OES.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: After receipt of a notification under paragraph (1), the competent authority must—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: assess what further action, if any, is required in respect of that incident; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: share the NIS incident information with the CSIRT as soon as reasonably practicable.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: After receipt of the NIS incident information under paragraph (5)(b), and based on that information, the CSIRT must inform the relevant authorities in a Member State if the incident has a significant impact on the continuity of an essential service provision in that Member State.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: After receipt of a notification under paragraph (1), the competent authority or CSIRT may inform—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the OES who provided the notification about any relevant information that relates to the NIS incident, including how it has been followed up, in order to assist that operator to deal with that incident more effectively or prevent a future incident; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the public about the NIS incident, as soon as reasonably practicable, if the competent authority or CSIRT is of the view that public awareness is necessary in order to handle that incident or prevent a future incident.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Before the competent authority or CSIRT informs the public about a NIS incident under paragraph (7)(b), the competent authority or CSIRT must consult each other and the OES who provided the notification under paragraph (1).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The competent authority must provide an annual report to the SPOC identifying the number and nature of NIS incidents notified to it under paragraph (1).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The first report mentioned in paragraph (9) must be submitted on or before 1st July 2018 and subsequent reports must be submitted at annual intervals.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The CSIRT is not required to share information under paragraph (6) if the information contains—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: confidential information; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: information which may prejudice the security or commercial interests of an OES.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Operators of essential services must have regard to any relevant guidance issued by the relevant competent authority when carrying out their duties imposed by paragraphs (1) to (4).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A RDSP must identify and take appropriate and proportionate measures to manage the risks posed to the security of network and information systems on which it relies to provide, within the European Union, the following services—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: online marketplace;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: online search engine; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: cloud computing service.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The measures taken by a RDSP under paragraph (1) must—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: (having regard to the state of the art) ensure a level of security of network and information systems appropriate to the risk posed;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: prevent and minimise the impact of incidents affecting their network and information systems with a view to ensuring the continuity of those services; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: take into account the following elements as specified in Article 2 of EU Regulation 2018/151—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the security of systems and facilities;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: incident handling;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: business continuity management;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: monitoring auditing and testing; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: compliance with international standards.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A RDSP must notify the Information Commissioner about any incident having a substantial impact on the provision of any of the digital services mentioned in paragraph (1) that it provides.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The requirement to notify in paragraph (3) applies only if the RDSP has access to information which enables it to assess whether the impact of an incident is substantial.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The notification mentioned in paragraph (3) must provide the following information—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the operator’s name and the essential services it provides;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the time the NIS incident occurred;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the duration of the NIS incident;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: information concerning the nature and impact of the NIS incident;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: information concerning any, or any likely, cross-border impact of the NIS incident; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: any other information that may be helpful to the competent authority.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The notification under paragraph (3) must—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: be made without undue delay and in any event no later than 72 hours after the RDSP is aware that an incident has occurred; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: contain sufficient information to enable the Information Commissioner to determine the significance of any cross-border impact.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In order to determine whether the impact of an incident is substantial the RDSP must—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: take into account the following parameters, as specified in Article 3 of EU Regulation 2018/151—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the number of users affected by the incident and, in particular, the users relying on the digital service for the provision of their own services;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the duration of the incident;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the geographical area affected by the incident;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the extent of the disruption to the functioning of the service;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the extent of the impact on economic and societal activities; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: assess whether at least one of situations described in Article 4 of EU Regulation 2018/151 has taken place.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: After receipt of a notification under paragraph (3) the Information Commissioner must share the incident notification with the CSIRT as soon as reasonably practicable.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: If an OES is reliant on a RDSP to provide an essential service, the operator must notify the relevant competent authority in relation to it about any significant impact on the continuity of the service it provides caused by an incident affecting the RDSP as soon as it occurs.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: If an incident notified under paragraph (3) affects two or more Member States, the Information Commissioner must inform the relevant authorities in each of the affected Member States about that incident as soon as reasonably practicable.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The Information Commissioner is not required to share information under paragraph (9) if the information contains—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: confidential information; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: information which may prejudice the security or commercial interests of a RDSP.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: If the Information Commissioner or CSIRT— the Information Commissioner or CSIRT may inform the public about that incident or direct the RDSP responsible for the notification to do so.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: consults with the RDSP responsible for an incident notification under paragraph (3), and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: is of the view that public awareness about that incident is necessary to prevent or manage it, or is in the public interest,
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Before the Information Commissioner or CSIRT informs the public about an incident notified under paragraph (3), the Information Commissioner or CSIRT must consult each other and the RDSP who provided the notification.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The Information Commissioner may inform the public about an incident affecting digital services in another Member State if—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the relevant authorities in the affected Member State notify the Information Commissioner about the incident;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the Commissioner consults with those relevant authorities; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the Commissioner is of the view mentioned in paragraph (11)(b).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The Information Commissioner must provide an annual report to the SPOC identifying the number and nature of incidents notified to it under paragraph (3).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The first report mentioned in paragraph (15) must be submitted on or before 1st July 2018 and subsequent reports must be submitted at annual intervals after that date.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In this regulation “EU Regulation 2018/151” means Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/151 laying down rules for the application of Directive (EU) 2016/148 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards further specification of the elements to be taken into account by digital service providers for managing the risks posed to the security of network and information systems and of the parameters for determining whether an incident has a substantial impact(a).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The Information Commissioner must co-operate with, and assist, competent authorities in other Member States, if the Commissioner considers that is appropriate to secure the effective supervision of—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: RDSPs who have network and information systems located in another Member State; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: digital service providers who do not meet the condition mentioned in regulation 1(3)(e)(i) but have network and information systems located in the United Kingdom.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The co-operation and assistance referred to in paragraph (1) may include—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: sharing information with, and receiving information from, a competent authority in another Member State to the extent that the Information Commissioner considers it necessary and appropriate;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: receiving a request from a competent authority in another Member State for the Information Commissioner to take enforcement action with respect to a RDSP mentioned in paragraph (1)(a); and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: making a request to a competent authority in another Member State for enforcement action to be taken with respect to a digital service provider mentioned in paragraph (1)(b).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The Information Commissioner must maintain a register of all RDSPs that have been notified to it.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A RDSP must submit the following details to the Information Commissioner before the registration date for the purpose of maintaining the register mentioned in paragraph (1)—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the name of the RDSP;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the address of its head office, or of its nominated representative; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: up-to-date contact details (including email addresses and telephone numbers).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A RDSP must notify the Information Commissioner about any changes to the details it submitted under paragraph (2) as soon as possible, and in any event within three months of the date on which the change took effect.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In this regulation, the “registration date” means—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: 1st November 2018, in the case of a RDSP who satisfies the conditions mentioned in regulation 1(3)(e) on the coming into force date of these Regulations, or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in any other case, the date three months after the RDSP satisfies those conditions.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In order to assess whether a person should be an OES, a designated competent authority may serve an information notice upon any person requiring that person to provide it with information that it reasonably requires to establish whether—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: a threshold requirement described in paragraphs 1 to 9 of Schedule 2 is met; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the conditions mentioned in regulation 8(3) are met.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A designated competent authority may serve an information notice upon an OES requiring that person to provide it with information that it reasonably requires to assess—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the security of the OES’s network and information systems; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the implementation of the operator’s security policies, including any about inspections conducted under regulation 16 and any underlying evidence in relation to such an inspection.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The Information Commissioner may serve upon a RDSP an information notice requiring that RDSP to provide the Information Commissioner with information that the Information Commissioner reasonably requires to assess—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the security of the RDSP’s network and information systems; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the implementation of the RDSP’s security policies, including any about inspections conducted under regulation 16 and any underlying evidence in relation to such an inspection.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Before a person is to be designated as an OES under regulation 8(3), a designated competent authority may serve an information notice upon that person requiring the person to provide it with information in order to assess whether to designate it.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: An information notice must—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: describe the information that is required by the designated competent authority or the Information Commissioner;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: provide the reasons for requesting such information;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: specify the form and manner in which the requested information is to be provided; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: specify the time period within which the information must be provided.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In a case falling within paragraph (1) the information notice may—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: be served by publishing it in such manner as the designated competent authority considers appropriate in order to bring it to the attention of any persons who are described in the notice as the persons from whom the information is required; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: take the form of a general request for a certain category of persons to provide the information that is specified in the notice.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A competent authority or the Information Commissioner may withdraw an information notice by written notice to the person on whom it was served.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: An information notice under paragraph (1) may not be served upon the SPOC or CSIRT.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A relevant competent authority in relation to an OES may— to assess if the OES has fulfilled the duties imposed on it by regulations 10 and 11.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: conduct an inspection;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: appoint a person to conduct an inspection on its behalf; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: direct the OES to appoint a person who is approved by that authority to conduct an inspection on its behalf,
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The Information Commissioner may— to assess if a RDSP has fulfilled the requirements set out in regulation 12.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: conduct an inspection;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: appoint a person to conduct an inspection on its behalf; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: direct that a RDSP appoint a person who is approved by the Information Commissioner to conduct an inspection on its behalf,
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the purposes of carrying out the inspection under paragraph (1) or (2), the OES or RDSP (as the case may be) must—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: pay the reasonable costs of the inspection;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: co-operate with the person who is conducting the inspection (“the inspector”);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: provide the inspector with reasonable access to their premises;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: allow the inspector to inspect, copy or remove such documents and information, including information that is held electronically, as the inspector considers to be relevant to the inspection; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: allow the inspector access to any person from whom the inspector seeks relevant information for the purposes of the inspection.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The competent authority or Information Commissioner may appoint a person to carry out an inspection under paragraph (1)(b) or (2)(b) on its behalf on such terms and in such a manner as it considers appropriate.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The designated competent authority for an OES may serve an enforcement notice upon that OES if the competent authority has reasonable grounds to believe that the OES has failed to—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: fulfil the security duties under regulation 10(1) and (2);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: notify a NIS incident under regulation 11(1);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: comply with the notification requirements stipulated in regulation 11(3);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: notify an incident as required by regulation 12(9);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: comply with an information notice issued under regulation 15; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: comply with—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: a direction given under regulation 16(1)(c), or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the requirements stipulated in regulation 16(3).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The Information Commissioner may serve an enforcement notice upon a RDSP if the Commissioner has reasonable grounds to believe that the RDSP has failed to—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: fulfil its duties under regulation 12(1) or (2);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: notify an incident under regulation 12(3);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: comply with the notification requirements stipulated in regulation 12(5);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: comply with a direction made by the Information Commissioner under regulation 12(12);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: comply with an information notice issued under regulation 15; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: comply with—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: a direction given under regulation 16(2)(c), or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the requirements stipulated in regulation 16(3).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: An enforcement notice that is served under paragraph (1) or (2) must be in writing and must specify the following—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the reasons for serving the notice;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the alleged failure which is the subject of the notice;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: what steps, if any, must be taken to rectify the alleged failure and the time period during which such steps must be taken; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: how and when representations may be made about the content of the notice and any related matters.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: If the relevant competent authority or Information Commissioner is satisfied that no further action is required, having considered— it must inform the OES or the RDSP, as the case may be, in writing, as soon as reasonably practicable.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the representations submitted in accordance with paragraph (3)(d); or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: any steps taken to rectify the alleged failure;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The OES or RDSP may request reasons for a decision to take no further action under paragraph (4) within 28 days of being informed of that decision.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Upon receipt of a request under paragraph (5), the relevant competent authority or Information Commissioner must provide written reasons for a decision under paragraph (4) within a reasonable time and in any event no later than 28 days.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The relevant competent authority for an OES may serve a penalty notice upon that OES if the OES was served with an enforcement notice under regulation 17(1) and the OES—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: was required to take steps to rectify a failure within a time period stipulated in the enforcement notice but the operator failed to take any steps or any adequate steps; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: was not required to take steps to rectify a failure but the competent authority is not satisfied with the representations submitted by the OES in accordance with regulation 17(3)(d).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The Information Commissioner may serve a penalty notice upon a RDSP if the RDSP was served with an enforcement notice under regulation 17(2) and the RDSP—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: was required to take steps to rectify a failure within a time period stipulated in the enforcement notice but the RDSP failed to take any steps or any adequate steps; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: was not required to take steps to rectify a failure but the Information Commissioner is not satisfied with the representations submitted by the RDSP in accordance with regulation 17(3)(d).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A penalty notice must be in writing and must specify the following—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the reasons for imposing a penalty;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the sum that is to be imposed as a penalty and how it is to be paid;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the date on which the notice is given;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the date, at least 30 days after the date specified in sub-paragraph (c), before which the penalty must be paid (“the payment period”);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: details about the independent review process set up under regulation 19 and how the right to review may be exercised; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the consequences of failing to make payment within the payment period.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A competent authority or the Information Commissioner may withdraw a penalty notice by informing the person upon whom it was served in writing.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The sum that is to be imposed under a penalty notice served under this regulation must be an amount that—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the competent authority or Information Commissioner determines is appropriate and proportionate to the failure in respect of which it is imposed; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: is in accordance with paragraph (6).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The amount that is to be imposed under a penalty notice must—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: not exceed £1,000,000 for any contravention which the enforcement authority determines could not cause a NIS incident;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: not exceed £3,400,000 for a material contravention which the enforcement authority determines has caused, or could cause, an incident resulting in a reduction of service provision by the OES or RDSP for a significant period of time;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: not exceed £8,500,000 for a material contravention which the enforcement authority determines has caused, or could cause, an incident resulting in a disruption of service provision by the OES or RDSP for a significant period of time; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: not exceed £17,000,000 for a material contravention which the enforcement authority determines has caused, or could cause, an incident resulting in an immediate threat to life or significant adverse impact on the United Kingdom economy.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In this regulation—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “a material contravention” means a failure to take steps, or any adequate steps, within the stipulated time period to rectify a failing that is described in regulation 17(1)(a) to (d) or (2)(a) to (e);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “enforcement authority” means the designated competent authority for an OES or the Information Commissioner for RDSPs.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: If an OES so requests, the relevant competent authority for an OES must appoint an independent person (“the reviewer”) to conduct reviews of a designation or penalty decision made by that authority in relation to that OES.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The Information Commissioner must appoint an independent person (“the reviewer”) to conduct a review of a penalty decision made by the Commissioner in relation to an RDSP, if the RDSP requests a review to be conducted.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: An OES may request the reviewer to review a designation or penalty decision made in relation to that OES in order to challenge any of the following matters—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the basis upon which the designation decision was made;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the grounds for imposing a penalty notice;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the sum that is imposed by way of a penalty notice;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the time period within which the penalty notice must be paid.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A RDSP may request the reviewer to conduct a review of a penalty decision made in relation to that RDSP in order to challenge any of the following matters—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the grounds for imposing a penalty notice;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the sum that is imposed by way of a penalty notice;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the time period within which the penalty notice must be paid.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Any request to conduct a review must—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: be made in writing, and copied to the relevant competent authority or the Information Commissioner, as the case may be;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: set out the reasons for requesting a review and provide any relevant evidence; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: be made within 30 days of receipt of the designation decision or penalty decision.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The relevant competent authority or the Information Commissioner must respond to a request, including to any reasons provided under regulation 19(5)(b), to conduct a review—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in writing to the reviewer, copied to the person who made the request for a review; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: within 30 days of receipt of that request.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The reviewer may extend the time limits mentioned in paragraph (5)(c) or (6)(b) if the reviewer considers it necessary to do so in the interests of fairness and having regard to the facts and circumstances of the particular case.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A request for a review suspends the effect of a designation decision or penalty decision until the review is decided or withdrawn.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The reviewer must uphold or set aside a designation decision or a penalty decision after consideration of the following matters—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the basis upon which the designation decision or penalty decision is challenged;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the response submitted under paragraph (6); and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: any relevant evidence.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The reviewer must provide reasons for the decision made under paragraph (9).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In this regulation—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “designation decision” means a decision to designate an operator of essential services made under regulation 8(3); and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “penalty decision” means a decision to serve a penalty notice under regulation 18(1) or (2).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: This paragraph applies where a sum is payable to an enforcement authority as a penalty under regulation 18.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In England and Wales the penalty is recoverable as if it were payable under an order of the county court or of the High Court.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In Scotland the penalty may be enforced in the same manner as an extract registered decree arbitral bearing a warrant for execution issued by the sheriff court of any sheriffdom.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In Northern Ireland the penalty is recoverable as if it were payable under an order of a county court or of the High Court.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Where action is taken under this paragraph for the recovery of a sum payable as a penalty under regulation 18, the penalty is —
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in relation to England and Wales, to be treated for the purposes of section 98 of the Courts Act 2003(a) (register of judgments and order etc.) as if it were a judgment entered in the county court;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in relation to Northern Ireland, to be treated for the purposes of Article 116 of the Judgments Enforcement (Northern Ireland) Order 1981(b) (register of judgments) as if it were a judgment in respect of which an application has been accepted under Article 22 or 23(1) of that Order.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: No action may be taken under this paragraph for the recovery of a sum payable as a penalty under regulation 18 if a review has been requested under regulation 19(3) or (4) and the review has not been determined or withdrawn.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A fee is payable by an OES or a RDSP to an enforcement authority, to recover the reasonable costs incurred by, or on behalf of, that authority in carrying out a NIS function in relation to that OES or RDSP.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The fee mentioned in paragraph (1) must be paid to the enforcement authority within 30 days after receipt of the invoice sent by the authority.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The invoice must state the work done and the reasonable costs incurred by, or on behalf of, the enforcement authority, including the time period to which the invoice relates.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: An enforcement authority may determine not to charge a fee under paragraph (1) in any particular case.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: A fee payable under this regulation is recoverable as a civil debt.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In this regulation—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: a “NIS function” means a function that is carried out under these Regulations except any function under regulations 17(1) to (4) and 18 to 20; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “enforcement authority” has the same meaning as in regulation 18(7)(b).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The sum that is received by a NIS enforcement authority as a result of a penalty notice served under regulation 18 must be paid into the Consolidated Fund unless paragraph (2) applies.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The sum that is received as a result of a penalty notice served under regulation 18 by—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the Welsh Ministers must be paid into the Welsh Consolidated Fund established under section 117 of the Government of Wales Act 2006(a); and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the Scottish Ministers or the Drinking Water Quality Regulator for Scotland, must be paid into the Scottish Consolidated Fund established under section 64 of the Scotland Act 1998(b).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Before a NIS enforcement authority takes any action under regulation 17 or 18 the enforcement authority must consider whether it is reasonable and proportionate, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to take action in relation to the contravention.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The NIS enforcement authority must, in particular, have regard to the following matters—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: any representations made by the OES or RDSP, as the case may be, about the contravention and the reasons for it, if any;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: any steps taken by the OES or RDSP to comply with the requirements set out in these Regulations;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: any steps taken by the OES or RDSP to rectify the contravention;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: whether the OES or RDSP had sufficient time to comply with the requirements set out in these Regulations; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: whether the contravention is also liable to enforcement under another enactment.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Any document or notice required or authorised by these Regulations to be served on a person may be served by—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: delivering it to that person in person;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: leaving it at the person’s proper address; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: sending it by post or electronic means to that person’s proper address.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In the case of a body corporate, a document may be served on a director of that body.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In the case of a partnership, a document may be served on a partner or person having control or management of the partnership business.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: If a person has specified an address in the United Kingdom (other than that person’s proper address) at which that person or someone on that person’s behalf will accept service, that address must also be treated as that person’s proper address.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the purposes of this regulation “proper address” means—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in the case of a body corporate or its director—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the registered or principal office of that body; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the email address of the secretary or clerk of that body;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in the case of a partnership, a partner or person having control or management of the partnership business—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the principal office of the partnership; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the email address of a partner or a person having that control or management;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in any other case, a person’s last known address, which includes an email address.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In this regulation, “partnership” includes a Scottish partnership.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The Secretary of State must—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: carry out a review of the regulatory provision contained in these Regulations; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: publish a report setting out the conclusions of that review.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The first report must be published on or before 9th May 2020 and subsequent reports must be published at biennial intervals.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Section 30(3) of the Small Business, Enterprise and Employment Act 2016 requires that a review carried out under this regulation must, so far as is reasonable, have regard to how the 2015 Directive is implemented in other Member States.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Section 30(4) of Small Business, Enterprise and Employment Act 2015(a) requires that the reports published under this regulation must, in particular—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: set out the objectives intended to be achieved by the regulatory provision referred to in paragraph (1)(a);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: assess the extent to which those objectives are achieved;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: assess whether those objectives remain appropriate; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: if those objectives remain appropriate, assess the extent to which they could be achieved in another way which involves less onerous regulatory provision.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In this regulation, “regulatory provision” has the same meaning as in sections 28 to 32 of the 2015 Act.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: This paragraph describes the threshold requirements which apply to specified kinds of essential services in the electricity subsector.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the essential service of electricity supply the threshold requirements are—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in Great Britain—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: electricity undertakings that carry out the function of supply to more than 250,000 final customers; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: electricity undertakings that carry out the function of supply, and generation via generators that when cumulated with the generators operated by affiliated undertakings would have a total capacity, in terms of input to a transmission system, greater than or equal to 2 gigawatts;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in Northern Ireland—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the holder of a supply licence under Article 10(1)(c) of the Electricity (Northern Ireland) Order 1992(a) who supplies electricity to more than 8,000 consumers; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: the holder of a generation licence under Article 10(1)(a) of the Electricity (Northern Ireland) Order 1992 with a generating capacity equal to or greater than 350 megawatts.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the essential service of the single electricity market in Northern Ireland, the threshold requirement is the holder of a Single Electricity Market operator licence under Article 10(1)(d) of the Electricity (Northern Ireland) Order 1992(a).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the essential service of electricity transmission, the threshold requirements are—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in Great Britain—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: transmission system operators with a potential to disrupt delivery of electricity to more than 250,000 final customers;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: holders of offshore transmission licences where the offshore transmission systems of that licence holder and its affiliated undertakings are directly connected to generators that have a total cumulative capacity, in terms of input to a transmission system, greater than or equal to 2 gigawatts; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: holders of interconnector licences where the electricity interconnector to which the licence relates has a capacity, in terms of input to a transmission system, greater than or equal to 1 gigawatt;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in Northern Ireland, the holder of a transmission licence under Article 10(1)(b) of the Electricity (Northern Ireland) Order 1992(b).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the essential service of electricity distribution, the threshold requirements are—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in Great Britain, distribution system operators with the potential to disrupt delivery of electricity to more than 250,000 final customers;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in Northern Ireland, the holder of a distribution licence under Article 10(1)(bb) of the Electricity (Northern Ireland) Order 1992(c).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Nuclear electricity generators and generators that are not connected to a transmission system are excluded from the threshold described in sub-paragraph (2)(a)(ii).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: Transmission systems for which an offshore transmission licence or interconnector licence applies are excluded from the threshold described in sub-paragraph (4)(a)(i).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In this paragraph—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “affiliated undertaking” has the meaning given by Article 2(12) of Directive 2013/34/EU(d) of the European Parliament and of the Council on the annual financial statements, consolidated financial statements and related reports of certain types of undertakings, amending Directive 2006/43/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council and repealing Council Directives 78/660/EEC and 83/349/EEC;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “distribution” has the meaning given by Article 2(5) of Directive 2009/72/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council concerning common rules for the internal market in electricity and repealing Directive 2003/54/EC(e), (“the Electricity Directive”);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “distribution system operator” has the meaning given by Article 2(6) of the Electricity Directive;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “electricity undertaking” has the meaning given by Article 2(35) of the Electricity Directive;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “final customer” has the meaning given by Article 2(9) of the Electricity Directive;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “generation” has the meaning given by Article 2(1) of the Electricity Directive and includes the generation of electricity from stored energy, and “generator” must be interpreted accordingly;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “interconnector licence” means a licence granted under section 6(1)(e) of the Electricity Act 1989(a);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “offshore transmission licence” and “offshore transmission” have the meaning given by section 6C(5) and (6) of the Electricity Act 1989(b), respectively;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “stored energy” means energy that—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: was converted from electricity, and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: is stored for the purpose of its future reconversion into electricity;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “supply” has the meaning given by Article 2(19) of the Electricity Directive;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “transmission” has the meaning given by Article 2(3) of the Electricity Directive; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “transmission system operator” has the meaning given by Article 2(4) of the Electricity Directive.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: This paragraph describes the threshold requirements which apply to specified kinds of essential services in the oil subsector.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the essential service of the conveyance of oil through relevant upstream petroleum pipelines, the threshold requirement, in the United Kingdom is the operator of a relevant upstream petroleum pipeline which has a throughput of more than 3,000,000 tonnes of oil equivalent per year excluding natural gas, if that operator does not fall within another threshold requirement in relation to this pipeline under this Schedule.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the essential service of oil transmission by pipeline, the threshold requirements are—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in Great Britain, operators of any pipeline with throughput capacity of more than 500,000 tonnes of crude oil based fuel per year; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in Northern Ireland, operators of any pipeline with throughput capacity of more than 50,000 tonnes of crude oil based fuel per year.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the essential service of the operation of relevant oil processing facilities, the threshold requirement in the United Kingdom is in the case of— an operator of a facility or pipeline with a throughput of more than 3,000,000 tonnes of oil equivalent per year.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: a relevant oil processing facility, or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: a relevant upstream petroleum pipeline which is connected to and operated from a relevant oil processing facility,
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the essential service of oil production, refining, treatment, storage and transmission the threshold requirements are—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in Great Britain, operators of any facility where that facility has a capacity greater than any of the following values—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: storage of 500,000 tonnes of crude oil based fuel;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: production of 500,000 tonnes of crude oil based fuel per year; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: supply of 500,000 tonnes of crude oil based fuel per year;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in Northern Ireland, the operator of a facility which has a storage capacity of greater than 50,000 tonnes of crude oil based fuel.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the essential service of the operation of petroleum production projects (other than projects which are primarily used for the storage of gas), the threshold requirement in the United Kingdom is, in the case of—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: a relevant offshore installation which is part of a petroleum production project (other than a project which is primarily used for the storage of gas), or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: a relevant upstream petroleum pipeline which is connected to and operated from such an installation, an operator of an installation or pipeline with a throughput of more than 3,000,000 tonnes of oil equivalent per year.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In sub-paragraph (5), the following are included within the description of the essential service—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: storage of crude oil based fuel;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: production of crude oil based fuels through a range of refining or blending processes, but excluding processes for rendering the oil suitable for transportation; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: supply of crude oil based fuels to retail sites, airports or other users within the United Kingdom.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In this paragraph—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “carbon dioxide pipeline” has the meaning given by section 90(2) of the Energy Act 2011(a);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “crude oil” means any liquid hydrocarbon mixture occurring naturally in the earth whether or not treated to render it suitable for transportation, and includes—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: crude oils from which distillate fractions have been removed, and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: crude oils to which distillate fractions have been added;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “crude oil based fuel” means any fuel wholly or mainly comprised of crude oil or substances derived from crude oil;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “foreign sector of the continental shelf” has the meaning given by section 90(1) of the Energy Act 2011(b);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “gas processing facility” means any facility which—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: carries out gas processing operations in relation to piped gas;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: This paragraph describes the threshold requirements which apply to specified kinds of essential services in the rail transport subsector.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the essential service of rail services the threshold requirements are—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in Great Britain, any operator of a mainline railway asset but excluding operators of—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: railway assets solely for the provision of international rail services;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: railway assets for metro, tram and other light rail, including underground, systems;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: heritage, museum or tourist railways, whether or not they are operating solely on their own network; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: networks which are privately owned and exist solely for use by the infrastructure owner for its own freight operations or other passenger or freight services for third parties and operators of passenger or freight services on those networks (including high speed rail services);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: in Northern Ireland, any railway undertaking in Northern Ireland.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the essential service of high speed rail services the threshold requirement in the United Kingdom is an operator of a railway asset for high speed rail services.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the essential service of metros, trams and other light rail services (including underground services), the threshold requirement in the United Kingdom is an operator with more than 50 million annual passenger journeys.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the essential service of international rail services the threshold requirement in the United Kingdom is an operator of a Channel Tunnel train or the infrastructure manager of the Channel Fixed Link.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In this paragraph—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “operator” and “railway asset” have the same meaning as in section 6 of the Railways Act 1993(a);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “international rail service” means a rail service where all carriages on the train cross a border of the United Kingdom and that of a Member State, and where the principal purpose of the service is to carry passengers or goods between stations located in the United Kingdom and a station in at least one Member State;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “mainline railway” has the same meaning as in the Railways and Other Guided Transport Systems (Safety) Regulations 2006(b);
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “railway undertaking” has the same meaning as in section 55 of the Transport Act (Northern Ireland) 1967(c) but excludes heritage railways operating solely on their own network; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “Channel Tunnel train” has the same meaning as in article 2(1) of the Channel Tunnel (Security) Order 1994(d) and “Channel Fixed Link” has the same meaning as in section 1 of the Channel Tunnel Act 1987(e).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the essential service of road transport services, the threshold requirement in the United Kingdom is a road authority responsible for roads in the United Kingdom that have vehicles travelling more than 50 billion miles in total on them.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the essential service of road services provided by Intelligent Transport Systems, the threshold requirement in the United Kingdom is a road authority that provides Intelligent Transport Systems services which covers roads in the United Kingdom that have vehicles travelling more than 50 billion miles in total on them, per year.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: (a) “road authority” has the same meaning in Article 2(12) of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/962 supplementing Directive 2010/40/EU of the European Parliament and the Council with regard to the provision of EU-wide real-time traffic information services(a); and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “Intelligent Transport Systems” has the same meaning as in Article 4(1) of Directive 2010/40/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council on the framework for the deployment of Intelligent Transport Systems in the field of road transport and for interfaces with other modes of transport(b).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: This paragraph describes the threshold requirements which apply to specified kinds of essential services in the healthcare settings sector.

text: in England, an NHS Trust as defined in section 25 of the National Health Service Act 2006(c) or a Foundation trust as defined in section 30 of the National Health Service Act 2006(d);

text: in Wales, a Local Health Board or NHS Trust as defined in the National Health Service (Wales) Act 2006(e);

text: in Scotland—

text: the Common Services Agency for the Scottish Health Service established under section 10 of the National Health Service (Scotland) Act 1978(f);

text: a Health Board, constituted under section 2 of the National Health Service (Scotland) Act 1978(g);

text: the National Waiting Times Centre Board established by article 3 of the National Waiting Times Centre Board (Scotland) Order 2002(h);

text: in Northern Ireland, the Health and Social Care Trusts within the meaning of “HSC Trust” in section 31 of the Health and Social Care (Reform) Act (Northern Ireland) 2009(l).
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: The threshold requirement which applies to the essential service of the supply of potable water in the United Kingdom is the supply of water to 200,000 or more people.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: This paragraph describes the threshold requirements which apply to specified kinds of essential services in the digital infrastructure subsector.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the essential service of Top Level Domain (”TLD”) Name Registries the threshold requirement in the United Kingdom is TLD Registries who service an average of 2 billion or more queries in 24 hours for domains registered within the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the essential service of Domain Name System (“DNS”) Service providers the threshold requirement in the United Kingdom is—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: DNS service providers with an establishment in the United Kingdom who provide DNS resolvers offered for use by publically accessible services, which service an average of 2,000,000 or more requesting DNS clients based in the United Kingdom in 24 hours; or
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: DNS service providers with an establishment in the United Kingdom who provide authoritative hosting of domain names, offered for use by publically accessible services, servicing 250,000 or more different active domain names.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: For the essential service of Internet Exchange Point (IXP) Operators the threshold requirement in the United Kingdom is IXP Operators who have 50% or more annual market share amongst IXP Operators in the United Kingdom, in terms of interconnected autonomous systems, or who offer interconnectivity to 50% or more of Global Internet routes.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: In this paragraph—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “DNS” is a reference to “domain name system” which means a hierarchical distributed naming system in a network which refers queries for domain names;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “DNS service provider” is a reference to “domain name system service provider” which means an entity which provides DNS services on the internet;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “IXP” is a reference to “internet exchange point” which means a network facility which—
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: enables the interconnection of more than two independent autonomous systems, primarily for the purpose of facilitating the exchange of internet traffic;
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: provides interconnection only for autonomous systems; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: does not require the internet traffic passing between any pair of participating autonomous systems to pass through any third autonomous system nor does it alter or otherwise interfere with such traffic; and
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf

text: “TLD Name Registry” is a reference to “top-level domain name registry” which means an entity which administers and operates the registration of internet domain names under a specific top-level domain.
source_document: KB 2/Europe/UK Network and Information Systems (NIS) Regulations 2018.pdf
